title: Peyara Remote Mouse
description: Build a phone touchpad and keyboard plus a WebSocket relay, with validated messages, reconnect logic, storage, and safe-by-default relay settings.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend Peyara Remote Mouse while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace event union, json encoding, decoding, bounds, and unknown-event rejection in its named source files.
Explain and trace panresponder deltas, click/scroll actions, text and key events in its named source files.
Explain and trace socket lifecycle, connection snapshots, exponential delay, max retry, and manual disconnect in its named source files.
Explain and trace host validation, settings key, asyncstorage adapter, and load/save flow in its named source files.
Explain and trace loopback default, bind acknowledgement, port/sensitivity validation, opt-in robotjs, event mapping in its named source files.
Explain and trace end-to-end protocol path, fallback logging, and evidence from isolated tests in its named source files.
Explain and trace safe defaults, trusted lan warning, robotjs native dependency, and shutdown/review in its named source files.
Explain and trace integration checklist, ui feedback, observable connection state, demonstration, and safe teardown in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
